newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks race to strong close, powered by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks race to strong close, powered by Wall St.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks raced ahead on Monday to close sharply higher after a strong rally on Wall Street on Friday spurred heavy buying in interest rate sensitive property and banking stocks, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index jumped 317.64 points, or 2.43 percent, to 13,399.34 after touching a session high at 13,439.78.
Turnover was HK$14.92 billion -- the fifth heaviest ever -- compared with HK$13.77 billion on Friday.
"Wall Street was strong and there is some switching out of red chips into property and banking and that is why the index is up," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
"I think the situation will continue. Resistance will be around the 13,600 level," he added.
The Dow industrials jumped 94.72 points, or 1.36 percent, to 7,071.20 on Friday, following the U.S. April jobs report and an agreement to balance the U.S. budget.
Analysts said U.S. April employment data had soothed some concerns about higher interest rates.
"You had a settling of nerves in the U.S. bond market," said Julian Ings Chambers, assistant director at BZW Securities.
"Providing you see continued strength in the U.S. market, and the bond market particularly, it probably is (sustainable)."
Shares of HSBC Holdings Plc led the market on Monday, crossing the HK$200 level for the first time in Hong Kong and hitting a record high at HK$204.00.
The stock closed at HK$202.00, up HK$4.50.
Property was the strongest performing sector.
"They are very interest rate sensitive," said Ings Chambers.
Analysts also said there were hopes a consolidation in the property market was coming to an end.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$2.75 to HK$73.50, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd added HK$3.00 to HK$90.50 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$3.00 to HK$70.50.
New World Development Co Ltd gained HK$2.80 to HK$48.50.

"You will probably see a bit of rotation out of what has been leading the market, out of red chips...into slightly more go-go stuff. Property is obviously a feature of today's market. That is the most notable laggard sector," said Ings Chambers.

Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd led the red chips lower, falling HK$2.80 to HK$40.40. A Hong Kong newspaper reported on Monday that parent Shanghai Industrial Investment (Holdings) Co Ltd was considering lowering its stake in the company.
